1f5187ba94.why: The 2-by-2 makes all four choices parallel and live, and it tests the shortening too; the hand-toward-the-shoulder hint is gone. The biceps lies at the front of the upper arm and its tendon inserts on the radius. Its contraction shortens the fibres and bends the elbow (with the brachialis), and the triceps straightens it. Muscles pull and cannot push. 'When the biceps works, the elbow bends' fixes the shortening case, so the lengthening (eccentric) pull is not a second answer. Human anatomy is this bank's lane.
